speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific skin lesion you are concerned about, including its location, size, and any changes you have noticed over time.

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) of the penis and finger. The presentation of a non-healing, crusty lesion in a 62-year-old male smoker with a history of failed treatments for syphilis and eczema, combined with the presence of a similar lesion on the digit, is highly suggestive of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. The patient's significant smoking history and age are major risk factors. Immediate biopsy of the penile lesion is indicated to confirm the diagnosis and rule out invasive malignancy.
